sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: This request seeks approval to purchase and commission a high-efficiency automated packaging line for the Dayton, Ohio plant to replace two legacy lines commissioned in 2008. The proposed equipment will increase rated throughput by 38%, reduce direct labor requirements by 9.5 FTEs, and lower unit conversion costs by an estimated $0.042 per case. Total project investment is $6.85 million, inclusive of installation, controls integration, and operator training. The initiative supports volume growth projections for 2027–2031 while generating a finance-grade, risk-adjusted return profile.

sections.heading: Operational Rationale
sections.body: Current packaging assets operate at 84% average uptime and have experienced escalating maintenance expenses, averaging $410,000 annually over the past three years. The new line incorporates servo-driven changeovers, inline quality inspection, and predictive maintenance diagnostics, reducing expected downtime to below 6%. Capacity will increase from 11.2 million to 15.5 million cases per year without expanding floor space. The upgrade also reduces material waste by approximately 1.8%, driven by improved sealing precision and automated rejection handling.

sections.heading: Financial Analysis and Return Metrics
sections.body: Base-case modeling over the 2026–2031 horizon projects incremental EBITDA of $2.05 million annually from labor savings, scrap reduction, and incremental contribution margin on added volume. After tax and depreciation impacts, the project yields an unlevered IRR of 21.4% and a simple payback period of 3.4 years. Using a 9.0% weighted average cost of capital and applying a 15% probability-weighted volume downside adjustment, the risk-adjusted NPV is calculated at $3.27 million. Sensitivity analysis indicates breakeven NPV at a sustained volume decline of 11%, providing a reasonable margin of safety.

sections.heading: Funding Requirements and Cash Flow Timing
sections.body: The total capital requirement of $6.85 million includes $5.9 million for equipment procurement, $620,000 for installation and utilities modifications, and $330,000 for commissioning and training. Cash outflows are scheduled across Q2–Q4 2026, with 30% payable upon order placement and the balance tied to factory acceptance and site commissioning milestones. Funding is proposed through a combination of operating cash flow and a $3.0 million draw on the existing revolving credit facility. The project does not require additional long-term debt issuance.

sections.heading: Risk Assessment and Mitigation
sections.body: Primary risks include integration delays, temporary production disruption during cutover, and lower-than-forecast demand in the Midwest distribution region. Mitigation measures include a phased installation plan, retention of one legacy line during ramp-up, and supplier-backed performance guarantees with liquidated damages clauses. A 5% contingency has been embedded within the capital budget to address unforeseen site modifications. Overall risk exposure is assessed as moderate and consistent with prior capacity expansion initiatives.

structure.full_text:
Capital Investment Request – High-Efficiency Packaging Line
Ref: CAP-26-117 | Date: 22 January 2026 | From: Michael R. Donnelly, VP Operations

Section Executive Summary
This request seeks approval to purchase and commission a high-efficiency automated packaging line for the Dayton, Ohio plant to replace two legacy lines commissioned in 2008. The proposed equipment will increase rated throughput by 38%, reduce direct labor requirements by 9.5 FTEs, and lower unit conversion costs by an estimated $0.042 per case. Total project investment is $6.85 million, inclusive of installation, controls integration, and operator training. The initiative supports volume growth projections for 2027–2031 while generating a finance-grade, risk-adjusted return profile.

Section Operational Rationale
Current packaging assets operate at 84% average uptime and have experienced escalating maintenance expenses, averaging $410,000 annually over the past three years. The new line incorporates servo-driven changeovers, inline quality inspection, and predictive maintenance diagnostics, reducing expected downtime to below 6%. Capacity will increase from 11.2 million to 15.5 million cases per year without expanding floor space. The upgrade also reduces material waste by approximately 1.8%, driven by improved sealing precision and automated rejection handling.

Section Financial Analysis and Return Metrics
Base-case modeling over the 2026–2031 horizon projects incremental EBITDA of $2.05 million annually from labor savings, scrap reduction, and incremental contribution margin on added volume. After tax and depreciation impacts, the project yields an unlevered IRR of 21.4% and a simple payback period of 3.4 years. Using a 9.0% weighted average cost of capital and applying a 15% probability-weighted volume downside adjustment, the risk-adjusted NPV is calculated at $3.27 million. Sensitivity analysis indicates breakeven NPV at a sustained volume decline of 11%, providing a reasonable margin of safety.

Section Funding Requirements and Cash Flow Timing
The total capital requirement of $6.85 million includes $5.9 million for equipment procurement, $620,000 for installation and utilities modifications, and $330,000 for commissioning and training. Cash outflows are scheduled across Q2–Q4 2026, with 30% payable upon order placement and the balance tied to factory acceptance and site commissioning milestones. Funding is proposed through a combination of operating cash flow and a $3.0 million draw on the existing revolving credit facility. The project does not require additional long-term debt issuance.

Section Risk Assessment and Mitigation
Primary risks include integration delays, temporary production disruption during cutover, and lower-than-forecast demand in the Midwest distribution region. Mitigation measures include a phased installation plan, retention of one legacy line during ramp-up, and supplier-backed performance guarantees with liquidated damages clauses. A 5% contingency has been embedded within the capital budget to address unforeseen site modifications. Overall risk exposure is assessed as moderate and consistent with prior capacity expansion initiatives.

structure.heading: Financial Case: ROI, Payback, Risk-Adjusted NPV, and Funding Requirements (2026–2031)
text_content: **Financial Case: ROI, Payback, Risk-Adjusted NPV, and Funding Requirements (2026–2031)**

The financial analysis for the proposed asset purchase presents three headline metrics that underpin the business case. Base-case ROI is 38% over five years (2026–2030). Simple payback period is 2.6 years from the 2026-03-31 commissioning date. Risk-adjusted NPV is $3.2M at a 10.5% discount rate. These outcomes reflect modeled cash flows, operating cost reductions, and capital allowances incorporated in the 2026 budget submission. Senior finance and operations reviewed sensitivities and agreed that these base assumptions are realistic for Board-level approval.

Detailed cash-flow projections separate 2026 commissioning costs from recurring benefits across the 2026–2031 horizon. Capital expenditure of $6.8M is scheduled in Q1 2026 with depreciation and tax treatment as outlined in the corporate capital policy. Expected annual operating cost reduction averages 9.4% versus the legacy line, and incremental gross margin improvement through higher throughput is modeled at approx. $1.1M per annum from 2027. Forecasts assume normal seasonality, with sensitivity scenarios adjusting benefits by ±20% to stress-test payback and ROI. Currency exposure is hedged per policy.

Risk analysis applied probability-weighted scenarios to produce a conservative valuation consistent with Board expectations. Scenario A (base operations) and Scenario B (lower throughput) were weighted 0.7 and 0.3 respectively to reflect execution risk, supply chain volatility, and demand sensitivity. Stress testing increased the discount to 12.5% in downside cases, reducing value but preserving positivity under base assumptions. Recommended governance actions include quarterly variance reporting, contingency triggers, and revised KPI thresholds tied to incentive payments. An independent review will be completed prior to first draw.

Funding requirements total $6.8M capex with an additional $0.6M allowance for commissioning and contingency across 2026–2027. Proposed funding mix: 1. internal cash of $2.5M, 2. a three-year term loan of $3.0M at market rates, and 3. vendor-supplied equipment financing of $1.9M. Draw schedule aligns with the 2026-03-31 commissioning date and milestone payments. The request to Treasury seeks approval for the structured financing, covenant terms, and a standby facility to preserve liquidity through the payback horizon. Board approval is requested at the May 2026 committee.

structure.full_text:
Capital Investment Proposal: High-Efficiency Packaging Line – Dayton, OH
Ref: CAP-26-117 | Date: 18 February 2026 | From: Manufacturing Finance & Operations

Section Executive Summary
This proposal requests approval for the purchase and commissioning of a high-efficiency automated packaging line at the Dayton, Ohio plant. The project addresses rising unit labor costs, capacity constraints during peak seasonal demand, and quality variability on the current Line 3 system installed in 2012. The total capital requirement is estimated at $8.45 million, with commissioning targeted for Q4 2026. Financial analysis supports a risk-adjusted return profile that exceeds corporate hurdle rates over the 2026–2031 planning horizon.

Section Operational Rationale
The existing packaging equipment operates at an average of 62 units per minute and experiences unplanned downtime averaging 9.8% of scheduled production hours. The proposed line, supplied by Kettering Automation Systems, will operate at 95 units per minute with automated changeover and inline quality inspection. This upgrade is projected to increase annual packaging capacity by 34% while reducing direct labor requirements by 14 full-time equivalents. Scrap rates are expected to decline from 3.1% to 1.4%, generating measurable material cost savings.

Section Financial Analysis and ROI
Total project cost of $8.45 million includes $7.6 million for equipment and installation, $0.5 million for facility modifications, and $0.35 million for training and startup support. Annualized gross savings beginning in 2027 are projected at $2.35 million, comprised of $1.1 million in labor savings, $0.8 million in scrap and rework reduction, and $0.45 million in maintenance and energy efficiency improvements. The base-case IRR is 18.7% with a simple payback period of 3.9 years. Over the six-year evaluation period, cumulative net cash inflows are estimated at $9.8 million.

Section Risk-Adjusted NPV and Sensitivity
Using a weighted average cost of capital of 9.2% and applying a 15% probability adjustment to first-year savings to reflect commissioning risk, the risk-adjusted NPV is calculated at $3.12 million. Sensitivity testing indicates that even with a 10% shortfall in projected throughput or a six-month delay in ramp-up, the NPV remains positive at $1.4 million. The primary risks relate to integration with the existing ERP scheduling module and supplier lead times; mitigation plans include a fixed-price installation contract and performance guarantees tied to throughput metrics.

Section Funding and Implementation Plan
Funding is proposed through a combination of $5.0 million in FY2026 capital allocation and $3.45 million in equipment financing under a five-year term at 6.1% interest. Installation is scheduled to begin in September 2026, with a four-week overlap period to maintain production continuity. Cross-functional oversight will be provided by Operations, Engineering, and Finance to ensure adherence to budget and timeline. Full operational stabilization is expected by January 2027, aligning benefits realization with the FY2027 budget cycle.
